about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

survivors.reason: WS-VARIABLES' first byte is WS-PGMNAME, which the port keeps as a typed Java field (initialState sets it to 'COTRN01C'); the image byte is never read

abended() runs caBack only for a LINKed task (level > 1); COTRN01C runs as a terminal task (level 1): for a terminal task the COMMAREA object is not observable (CICS discards it; linked_result drops it)
condition() answering -2 instead of -1 for a condition ignored by default: callers test only `to >= 0`, false for both

caWhole rebuilds DFHCOMMAREA's whole 32767-byte record around what the task left in its EIBCALEN bytes; COTRN01C reads DFHCOMMAREA only as DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN), at most the 218 bytes of its COMMAREA, which in_ writes from the caller's COMMAREA first, so the bytes the negation changes lie past them; for a terminal task the area's final contents are not observable (CICS discards them; linked_result drops them)
COADM01C never reads EIBDATE / EIBTIME (the header date and time come from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE), so EIBDATE cannot show
COTRN01C never reads EIBDATE / EIBTIME (the header date and time come from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE), so EIBDATE cannot show

a NULL attention key no longer sets EIBAID, which keeps its initial byte (a space); COTRN01C tests only ENTER, PF3, PF4 and PF5, so it takes WHEN OTHER exactly as NULL does (no scenario sends NULL, and the result would be the same)
a PF6 key no longer sets EIBAID, which keeps its initial byte (DFHEIBLK's image: a space); COTRN01C tests no key a space matches, so it takes WHEN OTHER exactly as PF6 does
a PF14 key no longer sets EIBAID, which keeps its initial byte (a space); it takes WHEN OTHER exactly as PF14 does
a PF17 key no longer sets EIBAID, which keeps its initial byte (a space); it takes WHEN OTHER exactly as PF17 does

caBack's fill_ at offset 1 for 0: caBack only writes the task's COMMAREA object back; for a terminal task that object is not observable (CICS discards it; linked_result drops it), and the RETURN carries out_'s copy of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA

s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond is non-null only for a COMMAREA longer than the 32767-byte DFHCOMMAREA storage (byte[] or link-area branch), which CICS cannot pass (COMMAREA is at most 32763 bytes), so the reset to null is a no-op.
a byte[] COMMAREA longer than DFHCOMMAREA's record is passed by no scenario (the det port is entered with a typed CarddemoCommarea object); only a caller with an over-long raw COMMAREA reaches it

survivors.before: s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond = raw.length > keep ? java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, keep, raw.length) : null;
survivors.after: s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond = raw.length <= keep ? java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, keep, raw.length) : null;
survivors.reason: the area beyond EIBCALEN is copied only when task.linkArea() is set, i.e. a det-port program LINKed COTRN01C with its COMMAREA's bytes; no CardDemo program LINKs COTRN01C (a terminal transaction, CT01, entered by XCTL)

Cutting s_DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN bytes (X23) matters only to a reference past EIBCALEN; COSGN00C never references DFHCOMMAREA, and the plumbing's own in_ (runs before the cut) and fill_ (runs after caWhole restores the full array) see the whole array either way, so cutting or not cutting is unobservable for every EIBCALEN.

Cutting s_DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN bytes (X23) matters only to a reference past EIBCALEN; COSGN00C never references DFHCOMMAREA, and the plumbing's own in_ (runs before the cut) and fill_ (runs after caWhole restores the full array) see the whole array either way, so cutting or not cutting is unobservable for every EIBCALEN.
at calen == the area's length the cut to EIBCALEN keeps every byte, so the branch's restore is a no-op; calen < length (user-signs-on-short-commarea) is the only case it changes anything
The IndexOutOfBoundsException catch is reached only by a reference past a COMMAREA cut to EIBCALEN; COSGN00C never references DFHCOMMAREA, and in_/fill_ run on the full array, so nothing throws it.

survivors.after: throw new DetCics.PastFrom("COMMAREA past EIBCALEN (" + calen + "Xbytes): not modelled");

survivors.after: /* lastLinkBytes = task.linkAreaTaken() && left != null ? java.util.Arrays.copyOf(left, left.length) : null; */

perform() reaches the outer-PERFORM scan only after a paragraph that is not its range's last returns; COSGN00C's PERFORMs each name one paragraph (from == thru) and MAIN-PARA (runTask's 0-5) always ends in EXEC CICS RETURN / XCTL / an abend, a Goback, so the scan never iterates and no PerformExit is thrown (this catch never runs).

perform() reaches this only after a paragraph that is not its range's last returns; COTRN01C's PERFORMs each name one paragraph (from == thru) and MAIN-PARA (runTask's 0-8) always ends in RETURN / XCTL / an abend, so `next >= 9` is never evaluated
WS-ERR-FLG is tested only through ERR-FLG-ON ('Y'); 'X' and 'N' are both not ON, and every path that sets the flag moves 'Y'

MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COTRN1AO on the first entry: without it the screen fields no program statement sets keep the image's spaces instead of low-values; the harness reads screen values with rstrip(' \x00') (equivalence_cics.py:2644, _same) and so cannot tell a blank field from a low-values one in the sent map
the 'Y' written on 'User not found' is never tested in this task (ERR-FLG-ON is read before READ-USER-SEC-FILE), and the next task starts from initialState's 'N'

MOVE SPACES TO TRNIDI before the READ: on a failed READ (transaction not found) the screen's TRNID keeps low-values from the RECEIVE instead of spaces; the success path overwrites it with TRAN-ID. The harness reads screen values with rstrip(' \x00') (equivalence_cics.py:2644, _same) and cannot tell low-values from spaces

`CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = LOW-VALUES AND = SPACES` for OR: every caller of RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN moves a program name into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM first ('COSGN00C', CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM when it is not blank, else 'COMEN01C', 'COTRN00C'), so it is neither, and both conditions are false

condition() returns a value only for a handled, ignored or ERROR-handled condition; COTRN02C sets no handler and an XCTL raises none ignored by default, so condition() throws (the abend) and `to` is never tested
inside `if (0 != 0)`-style dead branch: the paragraph's GO-TO result is only taken from a block the translator guards with the constant response 0 (SEND MAP has no RESP), so it never runs

survivors.before: DetCics.subfields(sub3, "PGMNAME", f61_PGMNAMEL, f64_PGMNAMEA, f190_PGMNAMEC, f192_PGMNAMEH, CS);
survivors.after: DetCics.subfields(sub3, "XGMNAME", f61_PGMNAMEL, f64_PGMNAMEA, f190_PGMNAMEC, f192_PGMNAMEH, CS);
survivors.reason: COTRN01C writes no attribute, colour or highlight byte for PGMNAME (it only MOVEs WS-PGMNAME TO PGMNAMEO) and never sets PGMNAMEL to -1, so subfields records nothing for it under either name
COTRN01C never reads EIBRESP2 (no reference in the source), so the zero stored after SEND MAP cannot show

a received TITLE01 (ATTRB=(ASKIP,FSET): the terminal sends it back) is stored in TITLE01I, the storage of TITLE01O; every SEND MAP follows POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, which MOVEs CCDA-TITLE01 TO TITLE01O, so the stored value is overwritten before anything reads or sends it
MNAME is ATTRB=(ASKIP,NORM) without FSET (COTRN01.bms): the terminal never sends it back, so RECEIVE never has it to store
COTRN01C never reads EIBRESP (no reference in the source), so the READ's stored response code cannot show

INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS (PF4 clear) without MOVE SPACES TO TRNIDI: the cleared screen's TRNID keeps low-values from the RECEIVE instead of spaces; the harness reads screen values with rstrip(' \x00') (equivalence_cics.py:2644, _same) and cannot tell low-values from spaces
